The flute is used mainly in traditional folk music, religious ritual and folk performance, and it plays a particularly important part in the gamelan ensemble.

巽他蘇林笛可聽見於巽他音樂的卡查皮蘇林合奏、德貢甘美蘭與巽他歌曲伴奏；在峇里音樂: The suling can be heard in kacapi suling ensembles, in degung gamelan and in the accompaniment of Sundanese song; in Balinese music it is an essential instrument of the gamelan line-up, and players use circular breathing to keep a continuous line of sound. There are listening contexts elsewhere in Southeast Asia too: at cultural festivals and other events in Brunei it plays with traditional instruments such as the gulintangan; among inland groups in Sabah and in Iban longhouses in Sarawak, Malaysia, men often play this flute; in the Philippines, Magindanao and other groups also use the suling as a common aerophone.
巽他蘇林笛屬氣鳴樂器，初學時先將吹口端靠近嘴部，對藤圈與竹管之間的小縫隙吹氣發聲: The suling is an aerophone. To begin, bring the blowing end to your lips and blow into the small gap between the rattan ring and the bamboo tube. Once the sound is steady, open and close the fingerholes to change the resonance wavelength inside the tube: the distance from the nearest open hole to the blowing edge sets the pitch you can play. At the same time, control the speed of the airstream and the shape of your mouth; double the air speed and the frequency of the pitch doubles. For a beginner the key points are an even airflow and clean opening and closing of the holes, then practise slides, moving between two notes without stopping the breath. More advanced players practise the pigeon effect, flicking a fingerhole open and shut rapidly to produce a sound close to a dove's call.
巽他蘇林笛為東南亞／印尼的氣鳴樂器，主要以長而壁薄的竹材製成管身；吹口附近以細藤: The suling is an aerophone of Southeast Asia / Indonesia, its body made mainly from long, thin-walled bamboo; near the blowing end a fine rattan strip is wound into a ring, leaving a blow hole. It sounds by way of the airstream passing through the gap between the rattan ring and the bamboo tube. The source does not record the materials of the other parts, nor mention a reed, wooden strip or any other material.
巽他蘇林笛音色溫潤柔和，具有獨特的東方韻味。其音質介於明亮與暗沉之間，帶有溫暖的: The suling's timbre is warm and gentle, with a distinctly Eastern character. Its tone sits between bright and dark, with a warm wooden quality and a slight nasal edge that make the sound restrained yet expressive. The instrument's range is comparatively wide: the low register is full and deep, the middle clear and open, and the top slightly sharp-edged but still warm. When it sounds, the resonance is concentrated inside the body of the flute and produces a natural overtone ring. Against the bright, piercing Western flute the suling sounds quieter and more elegant; beside the Chinese bamboo flute its tone is softer and rounder, without the dizi's carrying power. The instrument is particularly suited to delicate emotions and to the spirit of traditional Indonesian music.

Suling Sunda is the bamboo ring flute of the Sundanese people of Southeast Asia / Indonesia, an aerophone with the Hornbostel–Sachs number 421.211.12. Its body is made mainly from long, thin-walled tamiang bamboo, and the blowing end has a small hole ringed with fine rattan; the player sounds it by blowing into the gap between the rattan and the bamboo tube. It is used in the degung ensemble and is one of the main instruments of the kacapi suling ensemble, and it accompanies Sundanese song (Tembang Sunda); it is also an important instrument in Balinese music.
巽他蘇林笛（Suling Sunda）起源於印度尼西亞西爪哇地區，是巽他民族傳統: Suling Sunda originates in the West Java region of Indonesia and is an important instrument of the Sundanese people's traditional musical culture. The development of this bamboo transverse flute can be traced back to the pre-colonial period, and it is deeply marked by Indonesia's rich musical traditions.
隨著時間推移，巽他蘇林笛的製作技藝得以保留並代代相傳。20世紀以來，在文化保護運: Over time the craft of making the suling was preserved and handed down from generation to generation. Since the twentieth century, driven by cultural preservation movements, this traditional instrument has gradually gained attention in academic and artistic circles, and has become an important vehicle for Indonesian music education and international cultural exchange.
